messages:
maria (marketing): Hey team — we've got draft numbers for the launch blog and webinar. Can eng/runtime confirm methodology + re-run a few workloads for validation? Links and high-level metrics below. :rocket:

aj (eng/runtime): Can you paste the exact workloads, model/version, and config? Also need the benchmark script + random seed so we can reproduce.

maria (marketing): Sure — GDrive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1X-example (view only)
Workloads: marketing-demo-chat (conv), search-embed (512), summarization-longdoc (8k). Model: redwood-alpha-1b_v3 (fp16). Metrics: median latency 42ms, p95 120ms, tokens/s 950.

sam (eng/runtime): Quick notes — alpha-1b_v3 moved to kernel v12 last week; results differ vs v11. We should pin kernel and libcudnn tags. Also run both cold-start (one-shot) and steady-state (30s warmup).

aj (eng/runtime): Agreed. Can you upload the exact command lines? We'll re-run with:
```bash
./bench_runner --model redwood-alpha-1b_v3 --weights /mnt/models/alpha-1b_v3 --workload marketing-demo-chat.json --batch 1 --warmup 30 --seed 42 --kernel v12
```
Also run with --kv-cache-enabled true/false for chat.

maria (marketing): added bench scripts to GDrive and a tarball: gs://redwood-bench/marketing/marketing-workloads-2024.tar.gz

aj (eng/runtime): Thanks. We'll do a quick sanity re-run for the three workloads today (EOD) and post logs + diff. If numbers look off we'll schedule a full regression next week. Priority: marketing-launch.

ci-bot: Benchmark job queued: B-879. Runner: runtime-qa-05. ETA ~45m.

jess (product marketing): Amazing — please flag any caveats we should call out in the blog (kernel change, quantization differences).

sam (eng/runtime): Also capture system metrics (GPU util, PCIe stalls) and tokenization breakdown. If you can include a small sample of prompts we can validate prompt length distributions.

maria (marketing): will add sample prompts to the folder now. Thanks — ping me when results are in. :thumbsup:

aj (eng/runtime): Will do. I'll post the raw logs + a short summary thread in #eng-runtime when done.
